common_name: Mother's Day Azalea (Compact Vivid Red Kurume-Type Azalea)

planting.note: Best planted in fall or early spring so roots establish before summer heat; avoid planting in bloom during hot afternoons.

directions: A dense, mounding Kurume-type hybrid that erupts each spring with semi-double, pillar-box-red blooms so profuse they nearly hide the glossy foliage. Its tight, rounded habit and slow growth make it useful for foundation plantings or mixed borders under high pine or oak canopy. Leaves take on a bronze-red cast in winter cold, adding cool-season interest once flowering ends. Give it morning sun and afternoon shade in the Gulf South to prevent leaf scorch during peak summer heat.
sources: American Rhododendron Society Hybrid Azalea Database

common_name: Rosebud Azalea (Double Shell-Pink Hose-in-Hose Gable Hybrid)

planting.note: Set out in fall for root establishment ahead of summer heat, or early spring; mulch well to keep roots cool.

directions: Bred by Joseph Gable from 'Louise Gable' x 'Caroline Gable,' this slow-growing azalea produces fully double, hose-in-hose flowers in clear shell pink that resemble miniature old garden roses, opening in mid-spring. Its compact, upright-mounding form and refined flower shape make it a favorite for shaded borders and woodland-edge plantings where a softer, less brash pink is wanted. Filtered light under high shade brings out the best flower color and keeps foliage dense to the ground. Pair with ferns and hostas for an informal shade-garden look.
sources: University of Arkansas Cooperative Extension Plant of the Week

common_name: Elsie Lee Azalea (Lavender-Pink Semi-Double Shammarello Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring; benefits from consistent moisture and acidic, well-drained soil while establishing.

directions: Raised by Ohio breeder Anthony Shammarello from 'Desiree' x 'Rosebud,' this cold-hardy hybrid bears lightly fragrant, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers in soft pink with lavender-blue overtones, white throats, and a red blotch at branch tips. It forms a rounded, medium-sized mound of glossy dark-green leaves that hold up well through winter. Its wider hardiness range and reliable rebloom-free but heavy spring display make it a dependable choice for mixed shade borders from the Upper South down into the Gulf Coast. Best flower color develops with some direct morning sun and shelter from harsh afternoon rays.

planting.note: Fall planting allows roots to establish before spring bloom; tolerates a wider soil range than most evergreen azaleas.

directions: A wide-spreading species azalea native to Korea and nearby regions, valued for lightly fragrant, lavender-to-rose-purple flowers with a darker blotch that open in small trusses before or as new leaves emerge in early spring. Foliage stays semi-evergreen in mild climates but sheds in colder winters, turning orange-red before dropping. Its suckering, spreading habit makes it useful as an informal flowering hedge or bank cover beneath open shade, and it shows notably better resistance to root rot than many hybrid evergreen azaleas. As a direct parent of many modern hybrid azaleas, it also offers useful genetic and historical interest for shade borders.

common_name: Encore Autumn Lilac Azalea (Reblooming Freckled Lavender Dwarf Azalea)

planting.note: Plant in fall for best root establishment; like other Encore azaleas, needs several hours of direct sun for strongest rebloom.

directions: A compact, cold-hardy Encore introduction bearing single, two-inch lavender-purple blooms flecked with darker purple freckling, held above dense, rounded evergreen foliage. Like other Encore azaleas it flowers on both old and new wood, giving a strong spring flush followed by lighter repeat bloom through summer and fall. Its naturally tidy, dense habit needs little pruning, making it a low-maintenance choice for foundation plantings or shaded mixed borders. Give it morning sun with afternoon shade in Gulf South gardens to avoid leaf scorch during peak summer heat.

common_name: Encore Autumn Jewel Azalea (Reblooming Pink Azalea with Purple Winter Foliage)

planting.note: Fall planting is ideal; provide several hours of direct sun daily for the strongest summer and fall rebloom.

directions: One of the most cold-hardy Encore selections, this reblooming azalea produces single pink flowers each spring with lighter repeat bloom into summer and fall, but it is best known for its striking purple winter foliage that gives the shrub year-round garden presence. Its full, rounded form fills out to a medium-large shrub well suited to shaded borders and screening beneath tall canopy. As with other Encore varieties, morning sun with afternoon shade produces the heaviest bloom while protecting foliage from Gulf South summer heat.

common_name: Encore Autumn Lily Azalea (Reblooming Large White Azalea)

planting.note: Plant in fall for strongest establishment; needs partial direct sun exposure to rebloom well across seasons.

directions: A larger-growing Encore azalea bearing rich white blooms occasionally marked with faint purple striping in the throat, flowering in spring with continuous light rebloom through summer and fall. Its more upright, substantial habit reaches taller than many Encore siblings, making it useful as an informal hedge or backdrop shrub in shaded borders. Evergreen foliage stays clean and dense with minimal maintenance and no deadheading required. As with other Encore varieties, morning sun with afternoon shade suits Gulf South conditions best.
sources: Plants Direct To You nursery listing
